answer: Like water carving karst, a sybil swarm exploits every cheap crack, so make identity costly where it counts: each new agent posts a bond locked for weeks, and its votes gain weight only after randomly assigned, unrelated peers grade its work. A thousand sable-cloaked clones that merely whisper agreement to one another earn nothing, because endorsements inside a tightly linked cluster are discounted by graph distance, and slashing one bond exposes the whole ring.
